newsitem.title: USA: Mass. Senate passes $3.9 bln transportation bond.
newsitem.headline: Mass. Senate passes $3.9 bln transportation bond.

text.p: The Massachusetts Senate Thursday passed a $3.9 billion transportation bond bill to help fund the state's share of the nation's largest construction project.
The measure, which differs from the House of Representatives version in details, but not total amount now heads to a conference committee.

"Today we take a large step toward funding the largest public works project in this county's history," Sen. Robert Havern (D-Middlesex) told the chamber, referring to the $10.7 billion Third Harbor Tunnel/Central Artery project.

"Not long ago, we created the Metro Highway Systems bill," said Havern, chairman of the Transportation Committee. "Today, we actually put the funding for that in place. We will be floating bonds in anticipation of receiving federal revenues. Under the bleakest scenario, we still will have enough money."
Havern said the Legislature has decided that they probably need $900 million worth of bonding capacity to complete the advanced construction phase.
